title: Bringing AutoConfig to Polling Endpoints
summary: AutoConfig now works with Polling Endpoints. Declare and manage your polling endpoint in code. Start receiving events in a few lines of code.
body_markdown:
A few weeks ago, we[launched Webhooks AutoConfig](https://www.svix.com/blog/webhooks-autoconfig/) , a much easier way to set up and consume webhooks.


Now, we're bringing the same convenience to[Polling Endpoints](https://www.svix.com/blog/announcing-polling-endpoints/) . Polling Endpoints still had to be created and updated in the UI, separately from the worker that reads them. With AutoConfig, the endpoint configuration and the worker code can live in the same place and stay in sync.


## How to use it


In the Application Portal, webhook consumers can now select *Use AutoConfig* when creating a Polling Endpoint.


The portal will issue a token. It also contains the credentials for polling, so you don't need to wire in any additional keys. Pass that to` AutoConfigConsumer` and call` subscribe()` :


```text
import    {   AutoConfigConsumer  }    from    'svix'


const   consumer  =    new    AutoConfigConsumer  (  AUTO_CONFIG_TOKEN  ,    {
filterTypes :    [  'invoice.paid'  ,    'user.created'  ]  ,
}  )


await   consumer .  subscribe  (  )


```


Like AutoConfig for regular webhook endpoints,` subscribe()` creates or updates the endpoint with the given configuration.


## Polling for events


The` AutoConfigConsumer` instance has convenient methods to get batches of events and commit the processed ones, so the worker loop can be as simple as:


```text
const   consumerId  =    'my-consumer'
while    (  workerRunning )    {
const   msgs  =    await   consumer .  receive  (  consumerId )


for    (  const   msg  of   msgs .  data )    {
// Process msg.data...
console  .  log  (  msg )
}


if    (  msgs .  data .  length  >    0  )    {
await   consumer .  commit  (  consumerId ,   msgs .  data .  at  (  -  1  )  .  offset )
}
}


```


The Consumer ID is used to track progress, so the worker can pick up where it left off after a restart.


AutoConfig and Polling Endpoints can be enabled for your environment from the[Svix dashboard](https://dashboard.svix.com/settings/organization/general-settings) . It's included on all plans and supported in every Svix SDK language.


For more information, please refer to the[Polling Endpoints AutoConfig docs](https://docs.svix.com/receiving/using-app-portal/polling-endpoints#using-autoconfig) .


## Great for AI agents


Polling Endpoints and AutoConfig are also great primitives for personal AI agents like OpenClaw or Hermes.


With Polling Endpoints, you don't need to expose public URLs from your machine to the internet. They also guarantee your agent never misses an event and always processes events in order, even after being down temporarily.


AutoConfig provides a simple API agents can understand and manage on their own, so you don't have to deal with any manual webhook configuration. Give your agent the AutoConfig token, and it does the rest.


## Closing words


Polling Endpoints remove the need to expose a public HTTP endpoint to listen for events. AutoConfig lets you manage the endpoint configuration in code.


Together they make it easier to consume events, solving many of the difficulties that come with regular webhooks, like having to expose a public URL, verifying webhook signatures, or dealing with configuration drift.


We are excited about the possibilities that this combination opens up, and have many new things in the works to make it even more powerful!
